proposition: For the PG owner, RentOK is the cheat code that turns the five things that beat him every month — verification, rent, runaways, reconciliation, complaints — into the one power that clears them.

board.style_line: Original 16-bit-style side-scrolling platform game rendered as a full-bleed 9:16 screen capture: chunky four-pixel sprites, hard aliased edges, no anti-aliasing, flat limited palette of dusty cement grey and ochre with cyan #03FFF1 as the only saturated hue in frame, one flat frontal light, locked side-on game camera, no camera roll, no depth of field.
board.negative_line: no text, no letterforms, no numerals, no logos, no watermarks, no captions, no user-interface chrome; no red cap, no blue dungarees, no moustachioed plumber in overalls, no brick blocks, no question-mark blocks, no mushroom, turtle or goomba creatures, no castle, no coin-block motif; no reference to any existing game, film, character, actor or brand; no real person's likeness; no photoreal rendering; no motion blur.

identity_anchors.OWNER: the player character: a stocky Indian man of about forty-five, six sprite-heads tall, short black hair and a four-pixel black moustache, dark green half-sleeve shirt over grey trousers, brown sandals, a fat brass keyring on his left hip, bare-headed, no hat and no overalls.
identity_anchors.PG_TOWER: the level: a five-storey Indian paying-guest building seen side-on in cutaway, every floor a flat cement platform with a painted ochre dado stripe, steel-grille windows, a drying line of clothes on one balcony rail, and an open stairwell at the right edge of each floor.
identity_anchors.PHONE: the product surface: a slim dark rectangular phone held flat in the OWNER's right hand, screen square to the viewer, its face a deep blue #0038FF field that lights with cyan #03FFF1.
identity_anchors.OBSTACLE_SWARM: the five hazards, blocky pixel objects and never animals: a faceless grey key-shaped gatekeeper filling a doorway; a rolling boulder made of stitched coin-sacks; a running dark silhouette trailing a torn paper slip; a whirling storm of loose paper slips; and a squat red bell blinking on and off.
identity_anchors.CYAN_POWER: the power-up: a hard-edged cyan #03FFF1 beam leaving the PHONE screen, and a two-pixel cyan outline drawn around the OWNER's whole sprite.
identity_anchors.FLAG: the goal: a plain cyan #03FFF1 pennant on a thin blue #0038FF pole standing at the roof edge, no emblem, no device, nothing written on it.

hero_frame.description: The OWNER has stopped running. He stands square in the stairwell holding the PHONE flat at chest height, screen to the viewer, and a hard-edged cyan beam is leaving that screen and running the full height of the frame. The grey key-shaped gatekeeper is caught inside the beam mid-dissolve, breaking apart into a falling column of coins that curve back down into the phone. Four more hazards wait further right along the corridor, still whole but lit cyan for the first time, and the stairwell that was grey in every earlier beat is now lit end to end by the light coming off the phone in his hand. Nothing is written anywhere in the frame.

audio.music_bed: A dry original chiptune on square-wave and noise channels only: a hurried minor-key loop at about 150 bpm under beats 1-3, one full bar of silence across the cheat-code entry, then the same melody returned in major with a steady bass pulse from beat 5 to the end. No lyrics, no sung brand name, no jingle; the melody carries no message on its own. Sound effects are diegetic to the game world: sandal-fall thuds, a paper rustle, a bell, a coin cascade, a flag snap.

beats.title: Dues day
beats.feeling: The low, familiar dread of the third of the month: the viewer recognises being behind on something before he has worked out what he is watching.
beats.framing: Locked side-on game camera, no move. OWNER runs rightward along the second-floor platform of PG_TOWER, held in the left zone of the 9:16 frame so the corridor ahead fills the right two-thirds. PHONE dark in his right hand, keyring swinging. A thin grey dues bar sits high in the frame, draining left to right. Loose rent slips lift off the cement behind his heels. Whole frame in cement grey and ochre; no cyan anywhere yet, so the palette has somewhere to go.
beats.first_frame: The still at t_in: OWNER mid-stride, left sandal off the platform, mouth set, keyring lifted off his hip; the dues bar already three-quarters drained; two rent slips still lying flat on the cement behind him; the corridor ahead empty and grey; the PHONE screen black. Nothing has moved yet.
beats.impact: Camera stays still by choice, so all the motion is his. He runs the full 3.2 s and never gains a pixel on the frame edge — the level scrolls at exactly his speed, which is the whole joke and the whole problem. Chiptune enters on frame one in a hurried minor key; one low noise-channel thud on every sandal-fall; no music has been promised that the film will not keep.

beats.title: Two that block him
beats.feeling: Recognition sharpening into irritation — these are not invented monsters, they are this week.
beats.framing: Same locked side-on camera, same platform, screen direction still left-to-right. Two hazards from OBSTACLE_SWARM enter from the right: the faceless grey key-shaped gatekeeper standing immovable in a doorway at mid-frame, and behind it the coin-sack boulder rolling toward the OWNER. He brakes, skids, ducks under the doorway lintel. The dues bar drops two segments. Composited labels sit in the upper-centre zone over flat cement, one at a time, never over his face.
beats.first_frame: The still at t_in: OWNER's sandals skidding, a two-pixel dust puff at his heels; the grey key-shaped gatekeeper standing square in the doorway ahead of him, filling it; the coin-sack boulder just entering frame right, one third visible, still. The dues bar at two-thirds. The frame is entirely cement grey, ochre and black.
beats.impact: One cue per beat: the hazards move, the camera does not. The gatekeeper does not lunge, which is worse — it simply does not let him past. Boulder arrival carries a low noise-channel rumble that begins under this shot and is explained by the picture in it. Cut out on the boulder's roll, which motivates the departure.

beats.title: Three that finish him
beats.feeling: Being surrounded. The point where the month stops being work and starts being a pile.
beats.framing: Camera still locked, still side-on, direction held. The OWNER is backed into the right wall of the stairwell landing — the first time he has been on the right of the frame, and he got there on screen, so the side change is shown. Three more hazards close on him: the running dark silhouette trailing a torn slip crossing behind him, the whirling storm of loose paper slips filling the upper left, the squat red bell blinking at his knee. His sprite flashes white on alternate frames, the platform-game grammar for a life about to go. Dues bar empty. Composited labels enter in the upper-centre zone, one per hazard.
beats.first_frame: The still at t_in: OWNER pressed flat to the right wall, arms up, sprite caught on its white flash frame; the torn-slip silhouette frozen mid-stride behind him; the paper storm hanging in the upper left as a fixed spiral of slips; the red bell lit and still; the dues bar an empty grey outline; PHONE still black in his hand.
beats.impact: The shortest beat in the film, and the only one where three things move at once — the crowding is the point, and it is the gap this film has opened: he cannot win this level as it stands. Chiptune tightens a semitone; bell effect on the beat; the last frame of the beat holds one-sixth of a second on his flash, so the freeze that follows lands as a break, not a glitch.

beats.title: The cheat code
beats.feeling: The exhale of remembering there is a way out of this that other people already use.
beats.framing: The level holds — hazards stop mid-motion, slips hang in the air. OWNER lifts the PHONE from his hip to chest height, screen square to the viewer in the centre zone, and the screen wakes to a flat deep blue #0038FF field, the first non-grey in the film. Generated imagery stops at the blank blue screen: the supplied RentOK wordmark and every string are composited by code onto that screen, the wordmark untouched, Rent in white and Ok in cyan #03FFF1 on the blue ground. Composited cheat-code lines sit under the wordmark on flat blue.
beats.first_frame: The still at t_in: every hazard frozen exactly where beat 3 left it, paper slips hanging unmoving; OWNER's hand already at chest height, PHONE screen square to camera and blank deep blue; his face turned to the screen, not to camera; the rest of the frame unchanged cement grey. No light has left the phone yet.
beats.impact: Stillness chosen, not defaulted: the only movement in 3.6 s is the phone rising and the blue arriving. The music drops to one full bar of silence, so the room tone and the paper rustle are suddenly audible — the track is heard as if it were speech. A single descending square-wave arpeggio marks the install. Brand mark and name land at 9.6 s, inside ten seconds.

beats.title: Power
beats.feeling: The turn — relief with force behind it. Not rescue; equipment.
beats.framing: Hero frame beat. Camera locked, side-on, OWNER returned to the left-of-centre zone facing right, standing still for the first time in the film. CYAN_POWER leaves the PHONE as a hard-edged beam running the full height of the 9:16 frame, and a two-pixel cyan outline closes around his whole sprite — the immunity read. The grey key-shaped gatekeeper stands inside the beam, breaking into a falling column of coins that curve back down into the phone. The other four hazards wait further right, still whole, lit cyan along their left edges for the first time. Cement grey stays desaturated everywhere the beam does not reach, so cyan is the single saturated element and the product is what is saturated.
beats.first_frame: The still at t_in: the beam just born, two pixels wide at the screen and widening upward; the cyan outline half-drawn around the OWNER, closed at his feet and open at his shoulders; the gatekeeper whole but edge-lit cyan, its first coins not yet detached; the four further hazards in grey silhouette down the corridor; his stance square, weight on both feet.
beats.impact: The beat that has to sell the product with no words: the product is in use, in his hand, and the end result — the obstacle turning back into money — is happening in the same frame. No camera move; the colour does the work a move would do, and the colour was tied to the phone one beat earlier and closer, so it reads instantly. Music returns in major on the beam's first frame, channelling relief the picture has already made. Coin cascade on the noise channel.

beats.title: The run
beats.feeling: Momentum. The pleasure of watching a backlog get cleared in one pass.
beats.framing: Locked camera, level scrolling right at double the beat-1 rate; OWNER holds the left third of the frame and now gains on it. He runs through the coin-sack boulder, which bursts into coins against his cyan outline without slowing him; the torn-slip silhouette runs into the beam and dissolves; the red bell is caught mid-blink and folds into a single neat ticket that drops into the phone. Each hazard leaves a short cyan coin trail that follows him. Composited check lines enter in the upper-centre zone, one as each hazard falls, never two on screen at once.
beats.first_frame: The still at t_in: OWNER at full stride in the left third, cyan outline closed and bright, beam ahead of him; the coin-sack boulder one body-length away and already cracked along one seam; the torn-slip silhouette further right mid-run; the red bell lit at the far right of the corridor; a trail of six coins hanging in the air behind him.
beats.impact: The film's declared action passage, so shots run shorter than their describe-aloud time by intent and the cutting rides the chiptune's bar lines. Immunity is shown, never stated: hazards hit him and break. Three impacts land on three downbeats; each composited check arrives on the impact frame, so picture and text agree exactly.

beats.title: Everything in one place
beats.feeling: Order arriving. The specific quiet of a mess that has finished sorting itself.
beats.framing: The last hazard is the paper storm, and it is not shot down — it is collected. The whirling slips spiral down out of the upper frame and stack themselves into one lit column on the PHONE screen, which the OWNER holds up in the centre zone; the grey dues bar above refills left to right and settles full. Camera still locked. The corridor behind him, cleared, runs away to the right in cement grey while the phone and the stack are the only cyan in frame. Composited dashboard line enters in the upper-centre zone over flat grey wall.
beats.first_frame: The still at t_in: the paper storm caught halfway down its spiral, slips angled into a funnel that ends at the PHONE screen; the bottom four slips already flat and squared into a stack on the screen; the dues bar a quarter refilled; OWNER looking at the screen, sandals planted; the corridor behind him empty for the first time in the film.
beats.impact: The one hazard that could never be beaten by force is beaten by filing, which is the honest mechanic of the product and the reason this beat is not cut for pace. Camera holds its full 3.6 s because the stack has to be read. Music thins to the bass pulse alone so the paper settle and the single soft chime are audible.

beats.title: The flag
beats.feeling: Finished. Not triumph — the flat satisfaction of a month that closed.
beats.framing: Camera tilts up once, its only move in the film, motivated by the OWNER climbing the last open stairwell of PG_TOWER to the roof edge. He touches FLAG; the plain cyan pennant runs up the blue pole and snaps open. Behind him the grey sky field flushes to the brand's deep blue #0038FF, so the last generated frame of the film is already the colour the end card will be. PHONE still in his right hand, screen lit cyan. No text on the flag, none anywhere in frame.
beats.first_frame: The still at t_in: OWNER one step below the roof line, right hand extended toward the pole, cyan outline still faintly on him; the pennant furled at the base of the blue pole; the sky behind still grey; the cleared floors of PG_TOWER stacked away below him down the left edge of the 9:16 frame.
beats.impact: The film's only camera move, and it names its reason: an object in transit — him — across the location. The pennant snap lands on the last downbeat of the chiptune; the sky change happens inside one frame, so the colour cut and the musical resolve are the same event. Ends held, not cut, so the composed card can take over on a still frame.

beats.title: Brand close (code-composed)
beats.feeling: Plain instruction, offered to someone who has just watched why he would follow it.
beats.framing: No generated imagery at all. A code-composed card: flat blue #0038FF ground, the supplied RentOK wordmark file placed untouched in the upper-centre zone — Rent in white, Ok in cyan #03FFF1 — the ask beneath it, and the site line at the lower third. The cyan pennant from beat 8 is held as a small static pixel element at the top edge so the card reads as the same world, not a slide from elsewhere.
beats.first_frame: The still at t_in: the blue field already full, the wordmark already at final size and position, the ask lines and site line already set; nothing animates in or out.
beats.impact: Ends on the product, held three full seconds — longer than any word on it takes to read aloud, so it survives a sound-off feed and a fast thumb. The chiptune resolves on the card's first frame and stops; the film does not end on silence over a moving picture.

hazard_labels_first_pair.why: Each hazard is named on the frame where it first blocks him, one label on screen at a time, set in the upper-centre zone over flat cement so the pixels under the letters are one even value. The label makes the hazard legible to a PG owner in a sound-off feed; the picture already shows what it does.

hazard_labels_second_trio.why: Three names across 2.6 s, sequential and never overlapping, so the crowding is felt without any single line becoming unreadable. Same zone and ground as the first pair, so the eye already knows where labels live.

cheat_code.why: The brief's cheat code, composited onto the blank blue phone screen under the supplied wordmark, held three full seconds on a still frame. This is where the brand is named — 9.6 s, inside ten seconds — and it is the one moment in the film where the words are the event.

power_checks.why: One tick line per hazard, landing on the frame that hazard breaks: KYC as the gatekeeper dissolves (14.0), autopay as the coin-sack boulder bursts, dues-tracked as the runaway silhouette goes, complaint tickets as the bell folds. Each answers the hazard named earlier in the same zone, so the viewer reads a closed pair, not a feature list.

dashboard_check.why: Held alone over the beat where the paper storm stacks itself into one column on the phone — the only tick that matches a picture of filing rather than a picture of force, so it gets its own beat and the film's longest single-line hold.

end_card.why: The ask, on the pack, on a flat blue ground with the supplied wordmark above it and the site line at the lower third. Three seconds static: on a sound-off feed this is the only channel the ask has, so it is held far longer than reading it aloud would take.

mandatory.customer_words: The video has a Mario game.
mandatory.realisation: The whole 30 s is one continuous side-scrolling platform level with 16-bit-style sprites, a platform grammar of running, skidding, flashing on damage and a draining status bar — never a live-action film with a game bolted on.

mandatory.customer_words: The player is basically a PG owner.
mandatory.realisation: The OWNER identity anchor — a forty-five-year-old Indian PG landlord with a keyring and a phone, no costume, no mascot — is the only player sprite and is on screen in every generated beat.

mandatory.customer_words: The obstacles in the game are basically the problems that owner faces — tenant verification
mandatory.realisation: Beat 2: the faceless grey key-shaped gatekeeper that fills a doorway and simply will not let him past; labelled TENANT VERIFICATION; cleared by the beam at beat 5 against ✓ DIGITAL KYC.
Beat 2: the coin-sack boulder rolling at him from the right; labelled COLLECTING RENT; it bursts harmlessly against his immunity outline at beat 6 against ✓ AUTOPAY.
Beat 3: the running dark silhouette trailing a torn slip, crossing behind him; labelled LEFT WITHOUT PAYING; dissolved in the beam at beat 6 against ✓ DUES TRACKED LIVE.

Beat 3: the whirling storm of loose paper slips filling the upper frame; labelled NO RECONCILIATION; at beat 7 it is the one hazard not shot down — it spirals into a single stacked column on the phone screen against ✓ ONE DASHBOARD.
Beat 3: the squat red bell blinking at his knee; labelled COMPLAINTS; caught mid-blink at beat 6 and folded into one neat ticket that drops into the phone against ✓ COMPLAINT TICKETS.

mandatory.customer_words: The game also introduces a cheat code — install RentOK app.
mandatory.realisation: Beat 4 is the cheat code and the film's only still beat: the level freezes, he raises the phone, the screen wakes deep blue, and INSTALL / RENTOK APP composite under the supplied wordmark. The same two strings return as the closing ask on the beat 9 card.

mandatory.customer_words: Once it is done, Mario gets a gun sort of power/immunity.
mandatory.realisation: CYAN_POWER: a hard-edged cyan beam leaving the phone screen (the gun read) plus a two-pixel cyan outline around his whole sprite (the immunity read). Immunity is demonstrated, not claimed — at beat 6 hazards hit him and break while he does not slow.

mandatory.customer_words: It runs and kills all the obstacles
mandatory.realisation: Beats 5-7 clear all five in order: gatekeeper in the beam, boulder and runaway and bell on the run, paper storm collected into the dashboard. None is left standing when he reaches the stairwell.
Beat 8: he climbs the last open stairwell to the roof edge and touches FLAG; the plain cyan pennant runs up the blue pole and snaps open as the sky flushes to brand blue.

mandatory.customer_words: Platforms: Instagram Reels / Facebook and YouTube Shorts.
mandatory.realisation: Native 9:16 throughout, with the action in the vertical centre band, labels in one fixed upper-centre zone clear of platform overlays, and every point carried by picture plus composited text so the film plays with the sound off.
duration_s 30; nine contiguous beats, 0 to 30, the last a code-composed card of 3 s.

mandatory.customer_words: Game identity: An original Mario-inspired game, rather than an exact reproduction of Nintendo's character, artwork, music or game assets.
mandatory.realisation: The level is an Indian PG tower in cutaway, the player is a middle-aged landlord in a green shirt, the hazards are objects rather than creatures, and the score is an original square-wave chiptune. The negative line, repeated on every prompt, bars the cap, the dungarees, the plumber, the brick and question blocks, the mushroom and turtle creatures and the castle by name.

mandatory.customer_words: Power-up design: Delegated to the creative system, while preserving the requested game-style power/immunity mechanic.
mandatory.realisation: The power-up is the app's own light: a beam out of the phone screen and an immunity outline in the brand cyan — designed here, but keeping the requested mechanic intact, acquired at one moment and then held for the rest of the level.

mandatory.customer_words: Brand and product source: Official RentOK website, https://rentok.com.
mandatory.realisation: The supplied wordmark file is placed untouched at beats 4 and 9 — Rent in white, Ok in cyan #03FFF1, on the blue #0038FF ground — never generated, never redrawn, never recoloured; RENTOK.COM closes the card.

mandatory.customer_words: Visual treatment: Delegated to the creative system.
mandatory.realisation: Chosen and fixed in the style line: chunky aliased 16-bit sprites, a desaturated cement-and-ochre level so that cyan is the only saturated hue in the film and it belongs to the product.

mandatory.customer_words: exact_text_strings (fifteen supplied overlay strings, may_reflow false)
mandatory.realisation: All fifteen appear, verbatim, character for character including the tick glyphs, every one composited by code onto a flat measured ground; no string is generated as pixels and no prompt quotes a word to render.

brand_timeline.in_context: The product surface is on screen from frame one — the PHONE is in the OWNER's right hand in every generated beat, dark and useless through beats 1-3, which is the story. The supplied wordmark itself first appears at 9.6 s on that phone's screen, in his hand, inside the level; the brand cyan then spreads out of the phone from beat 5 and is the only saturated colour in every remaining frame. The mark returns on the closing card at 27.0 s.
brand_timeline.spoken: none — the film carries no dialogue and no voice-over, so the name is never said aloud. It is carried twice on screen instead, at 9.6 s and at 27.0 s, both times as the supplied mark plus the composited words.

last_frame: The code-composed card: flat blue #0038FF, the supplied RentOK wordmark untouched in the upper-centre zone, INSTALL / RENTOK APP beneath it, RENTOK.COM at the lower third, and the small cyan pennant from beat 8 static at the top edge. The film ends on the pack.

deviations.from: / default: set out to be interesting, not funny; no cartoon for adults and no comic register on a money category.
deviations.brief_clause: "The video has a Mario game. The player is basically a PG owner. The obstacles in the game are basically the problems that owner faces" — the customer has specified a game-cartoon register for an adult commercial audience, so the default is overridden. The brake is kept: the joke carries the selling point in every beat (each hazard is a real line item, each clearance a real feature) and nothing is slapstick.

deviations.from: / default: pair every on-screen CTA and brand mention with a voice-over saying the same words; supers equal spoken words.
deviations.brief_clause: The standing production constraint "no dialogue or voice-over", plus "Platforms: Instagram Reels / Facebook and YouTube Shorts", where autoplay is sound-off. The pairing is impossible and its premise (audio is heard) does not hold, so the on-screen channel carries ask and brand alone; the corpus states no rule for this case and the film is built to pass muted.

deviations.from: / default: the brand is present from the start and never lapses; name within ten seconds.
deviations.brief_clause: "The game also introduces a cheat code — install RentOK app. Once it is done..." — the brief's own structure requires the problem gauntlet before the brand can enter. Declared honestly: the product surface (the phone) is in hand from frame one, but the mark and name do not appear until 9.6 s. The ten-second bound is kept; the never-lapsing bound is not, and this is the deviation.

deviations.from: / default: no running line in all capitals; all-caps is the hardest read.
deviations.brief_clause: exact_text_strings supplies all fifteen strings in capitals with "may_reflow": false, so casing cannot be changed. Mitigated: no string is a running line — the longest is three words — each is set large, heavy and unrounded, one at a time, over a flat measured ground.

deviations.from: / default: a borrowed fixed-meaning image is cliché unless re-angled to the product's advantage; coded forms must be dated and scoped.
deviations.brief_clause: "An original Mario-inspired game, rather than an exact reproduction" — the platform-game code is borrowed deliberately. The re-angle is stated: the code is re-aimed so that the level is the owner's month, the hazards are his actual line items, and the power-up is the product doing its literal job, not a metaphor laid beside a logo.
